subject: HelixAI dedicated capacity — commit scenarios and thermal headroom
messages:
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Samantha Liu <samantha@helixai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-21T09:12:00Z
Subject: HelixAI dedicated capacity — commit scenarios and thermal headroom

Hi Samantha,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to hear about the increased batch/stream mix you're seeing in production. Attached is a short scenario analysis and cost model with three options we discussed for dedicated capacity to cover the next 12 months. High-level options in the spreadsheet: 

- Option A: Short-term burst (20 GPUs) for 12 weeks, then re-evaluate. Lower immediate uplift cost, good for seasonal spikes.
- Option B: Staged steady-state (add 10 GPUs now, +10 GPUs at Q4 milestone). Smooths spend, preserves headroom.
- Option C: Commit lift (additional 30 GPUs reserved annual) with discounted unit price and SLA uplift. Best for predictable scale and lowest unit cost.

One thing you raised that I asked our infra team to double-check is "thermal headroom" — in our dedicated model we can schedule GPUs across racks with varied cooling profiles; that influences how many nodes we can safely co-locate in a single physical cage without maintenance risks. The annex calls out safe packing densities and recommended maintenance windows.

Can you confirm a) whether procurement lead-time for PO/contract is 4–6 weeks, and b) any hard constraints around maintenance windows (e.g., weekend-only changes)? If helpful, we can model a hybrid: 10-GPU immediate add + 20-GPU commit with a 60-day ramp to accommodate procurement.

Next steps I suggest: you review the attached scenario_cost_model.xlsx and we schedule a short call with Karthik (solutions) and Marissa (renewals) to lock timing. If that plan works, I can route an amendment for signatures.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

Attachments: helixai_capacity_annex_v2.pdf (pdf), scenario_cost_model.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Samantha Liu <samantha@helixai.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: HelixAI Procurement <procurement@helixai.com>
Date: 2027-08-21T14:03:00Z
Subject: Re: HelixAI dedicated capacity — commit scenarios and thermal headroom

Ben — thanks for the options and the clear write-up. A few clarifications from our side before we loop in procurement: 

- Usage profile: Our monthly median sustained GPU-hours in production is ~26,000 GPU-hours; 95th percentile monthly spikes have pushed us to ~48,000 GPU-hours. Peak-serving latency SLOs are 95th <= 180ms for user-facing models.
- Preference: we prefer steady-state predictability, but finance is comfortable with a staged approach if the pricing delta vs immediate commit is documented.
- Procurement: PO lead time is typically 3–5 weeks but can extend to 8 weeks if we require a legal amendment.
- Maintenance windows: we can accept weekday maintenance between 02:00–05:00 PT but prefer weekends for anything longer than 4 hours. We also need a short SLA note about planned maintenance windows affecting burst allocations.

Thermal question: we run some model training on-prem, but for the Dedicated instance this will be in Redwood-managed racks. Please confirm that you will not co-locate extra high-power cards from other tenants in the same cage beyond the annex recommendations. That was a concern from our infra team.

I'll review the spreadsheet and should be able to push for a PO if you can provide the staged pricing and the amendment language.

Best,
Samantha Liu
Head of Platform Engineering, HelixAI
samantha@helixai.com
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: 2027-08-22T11:27:00Z
Subject: RE: HelixAI dedicated capacity — commit scenarios and thermal headroom

Thanks Ben — looping Karthik in for infra sizing and Karthik, quick notes from the customer:

- They provided 95th percentile spike numbers and a weekday maintenance window option (02:00–05:00 PT).
- Procurement lead-time is variable (3–8 weeks).
- They explicitly requested we avoid aggressive co-location in the same cage beyond recommended packing densities in the annex.

Karthik — can you validate the safety packing densities and give a recommended rollout plan that minimizes thermal churn? Specifically: 

1) If we do a 10 now + 10 later plan, can we guarantee the second tranche will be colocated in a different power/thermal domain to avoid rebalancing during a peak week?
2) For the 20-GPU burst option, what monitoring hooks do we want to add (temp sensors, rack-level throttling alerts) so we can commit to a 4-hour rollback SLA in case of thermal events?

I've attached a short annex I edited to include a maintenance note we can put into the amendment (see helixai_capacity_annex_v2.pdf). I also added a draft pricing row to scenario_cost_model.xlsx for staged vs commit comparisons. If Karthik signs off, we can hand this to Finance for a clean amendment and then route to DocuSign.

Marissa Cole
Renewals Director, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: helixai_capacity_annex_v2.pdf (pdf)
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Samantha Liu <samantha@helixai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, HelixAI Procurement <procurement@helixai.com>
Date: 2027-08-24T16:05:00Z
Subject: RE: HelixAI dedicated capacity — commit scenarios and thermal headroom

Samantha — thanks for the fast turnaround and the clear constraints. Quick summary and mutual action plan so we have the sequence in writing:

1) Technical: Redwood confirms we will not exceed the packing densities in the annex and will reserve a separate thermal domain for the second tranche where possible. Karthik has agreed to add temperature/thermal alerts and a 4-hour rollback playbook for burst allocations.
2) Commercial: Ben (me) will issue a staged amendment (10 GPUs immediate + option to add 20 GPUs at Q4 with 30-day notice). Pricing rows are in the spreadsheet; the staged price and the commit price are both shown with unit economics and expected monthly token cost.
3) Procurement / Timing: We will target PO in 3–6 weeks. Marissa will shepherd the amendment with Finance. Once PO is in, Redwood will schedule the initial 10-GPU rollout during your preferred weekday maintenance window (02:00–05:00 PT) or weekend if you request longer maintenance.

Action items:
- Ben: send DocuSign amendment link and finalize pricing table (today).
- Karthik: upload monitoring checklist and runbook (by EOD tomorrow).
- Samantha / HelixAI: confirm procurement lead-time and whether they want weekend maintenance for the initial rollout.

I have uploaded the amendment to DocuSign and included the link in the related links list — procurement can sign when ready. Attaching the amendment stub and the cost model in case you want to circulate.

Thanks all — excited to get HelixAI scaled reliably.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

Attachments: docusign_amendment_link.txt (link), scenario_cost_model.xlsx (xlsx)
